_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the primary head term for the JA font converter tool (title, H1, WebApplication schema alternateName). This is the term real users type into font-conversion sites per Chiebukuro answers that recommend 'フォント変換サイト'.
phrases.good_example: フォント変換 — かわいい・おしゃれな文字にコピペで変換（無料）

phrases.usage_guidance: This is THE central Japan-specific pain point flagged in prior research, and it is well-covered as an FAQ answer across many pages — but there is NO dedicated /ja/answers/ page targeting '文字化け' as its own zero-click query the way namae-shikaku-hyouji-riyuu covers the boxes/? symptom. Treat 文字化け and 豆腐/四角表示 (JA-009) as the same underlying phenomenon described from two angles (technical cause vs. visual symptom) and consider whether they need a unified answer page.

phrases.avoid_when: n/a — accurate technical usage throughout

phrases.usage_guidance: Correctly used and explained parenthetically ('豆腐（tofu）と呼ばれる現象') rather than assumed-known — good practice since this is community jargon, not universal vocabulary. Keep introducing it this way rather than using it unglossed.
phrases.good_example: これは豆腐（tofu）と呼ばれる現象で、決めているのは相手側の端末であってあなたの端末ではありません

phrases.english_concept: misattributing a Discord feature (spoiler tag) as text corruption
phrases.content_surface: not on any live ja/ page
phrases.usage_guidance: This is a genuine, distinct Discord-specific pain point separate from true mojibake/tofu: kaomoji strings that happen to contain double-pipe (||) sequences (e.g. 'il||li') get accidentally spoiler-masked by Discord's markdown, not corrupted. A JA answer/FAQ item correcting this specific misconception ('it's not mojibake, it's Discord's spoiler formatting — avoid || in kaomoji you paste into Discord, or escape it') would be a precise, evidence-backed addition distinct from the general 文字化け/四角 coverage already on site.
phrases.good_example: 以前discordでil||li(っω-`｡)il||li←この顔文字を送ったらなぜか黒塗り？になったのですがなぜですか
phrases.avoid_when: don't conflate with true 文字化け/tofu content — this needs its own explanation since the mechanism is completely different (markdown formatting, not missing glyphs)

Both are valid but should not be treated as interchangeable; a 'how to make kaomoji always work' answer page would naturally cover 単語登録 as the durable fix to the paste-failure problem in JTBD-16.

These are outside game-rules.js's current RULES table and outside the answer page's current game list, suggesting real additional per-game coverage demand beyond what's already served.

phrases.good_example: 2002〜2003年ごろに登場した、日本の女子中高生を中心に流行した文字装飾です。
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Correctly used for Roblox's actual in-app error framing ('対応していない文字'). Distinct register from the more community-slang '対応不可' (JA-014) used specifically by 荒野行動 players — both are natural but belong to different platforms' own vocabulary, keep them separate rather than treating as interchangeable.
phrases.good_example: Robloxは表示名もユーザー名と同じチェックにかけ、ほとんどの装飾されたUnicode文字を「対応していない文字」として拒否します。

phrases.native_phrase: 文字を円形に配置する / アーチ状
phrases.transliteration: moji o enkei ni haichi suru / āchi-jō
phrases.english_concept: arranging text along a circle or an arch (for a logo / emblem)
phrases.usage_guidance: Phrase Japanese headings as an action ('文字を円形に配置する方法') rather than as a noun label. Use '円形テキスト' only where you are naming the tool/feature itself, and 'アーチ状' for the half-circle. Naming the logo/emblem outcome ('ロゴ', 'エンブレム風') in the same sentence matches how JA tutorials frame the job.
phrases.good_example: 文字を円形に配置する方法 — アーチ状の上下を組み合わせて、ロゴのような円形デザインを作れます。
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'カーブテキスト' or 'カーブドテキスト' — katakana-Anglicism forms that read as unedited translation. Do not use 'パス上文字' outside a pro-tool context; it means nothing to a casual user.

phrases.native_phrase: 縦書き / 縦書き変換
phrases.english_concept: vertical writing — BOTH the genuine Japanese writing mode and the SNS one-character-per-line trick
phrases.register: neutral — spans literary/typographic and casual SNS use
phrases.content_surface: h1, title, meta, faq, tool copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Head term for the Japanese vertical-text page is '縦書き'; the tool-intent query is '縦書き変換'. The FAQ must be honest that the output is 疑似縦書き (pseudo-vertical, made of line breaks), not true vertical layout — Japanese users will notice, and saying it plainly is exactly the credibility a machine-translated competitor cannot fake. Do NOT describe it as a decorative trick in the way Latin-locale copy does; in Japanese it is a legitimate way to post a poem.
phrases.good_example: 縦書き変換ツール：1文字ずつ自動で改行し、SNSやLINEにそのまま貼り付けられる縦書き形式にします。
phrases.avoid_when: Do not reuse Latin-locale framing ('a fun way to stack your name') for Japanese — it misreads a native writing mode as a gimmick. Do not claim it is true 縦組み typography; it is 疑似縦書き.

phrases.native_phrase: 縦書き用の記号（伸ばし棒・括弧）
phrases.english_concept: punctuation that must be swapped for its vertical form when text is set vertically (the Japanese-specific breakage)
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the Japanese-side quality bar for a vertical-text feature. Either implement the substitution and say so ('伸ばし棒（ー）や括弧（「」）を縦書き用の記号に自動で置き換えます'), or state plainly in the FAQ that it is not applied. Silence here is what marks a page as translated-from-English. The equivalent boundary in Arabic is P14 and in Thai is P16.
phrases.good_example: 縦書きにすると伸ばし棒（ー）や括弧（「」）が横向きのままになります。縦書き用の記号に置き換えると自然に見えます。
phrases.avoid_when: Not relevant to Latin-script locales at all — never translate this FAQ into es/pt/de/fr/it/nl/pl as if it applied there. Keep out of title/H1; it is a body/FAQ detail.

phrases.english_concept: the # sign — Japanese names, and the same #/♯ confusion as Korean
phrases.register: '井桁' formal/typographic; 'シャープ' everyday spoken, including telephone-system usage
phrases.usage_guidance: On a Japanese # page, use 井桁 as the reference name and シャープ as the reading people know, then carry the #/♯ distinction as an explicit section — the Japanese Wikipedia article makes the point that they are 別の記号 (different symbols), so the page has a factual, citable job to do rather than just listing a glyph.
phrases.good_example: 「#」は井桁（いげた）と呼ばれ、電話の「シャープダイヤル」のようにシャープと読まれることもありますが、音楽の♯とは別の記号です。
phrases.avoid_when: Do not label ♯ as 井桁 or # as the musical sharp. Do not use ハッシュタグ for the bare character — that is the social-media label. 井桁 in a non-typographic context reads as the architectural/heraldic pattern, so keep it inside symbol-reference copy.

phrases.usage_guidance: Write 「見出し（ヘッドライン）」 on first mention exactly as Japanese sources do, then use whichever suits the sentence. This dual form is the natural Japanese convention, not redundancy.
phrases.good_example: LinkedInプロフィールの名前の下に表示される「見出し（ヘッドライン / Headline）」
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use ヘッドライン alone in copy that is meant to match the product UI, and do not use 見出し alone in a page title aimed at search. Do not mix in JA aesthetic/gaming vocabulary (JA-002 おしゃれ文字, JA-016 量産型) — completely wrong register.

phrases.english_concept: characters banned from job-application forms because they do not render across systems
phrases.register: formal/administrative; used verbatim in platform help pages and error messages
phrases.content_surface: faq heading, body copy, tool-side warning
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the single strongest professional-register finding of this pass and the most important boundary marker for Japanese copy: it is the locally-evidenced reason styled/special characters must never be offered for a Japanese job-application context. Use it in an honest 'where this does not work' FAQ.
phrases.good_example: マイナビ転職では、特定の機種、OSでしか表示できない文字（機種依存文字）を使用することができません。
phrases.avoid_when: Never use it as a selling point or a style category. Never suggest a workaround for a platform that has explicitly banned these characters — the correct guidance is 他の文字に変換する (convert to other characters).

phrases.native_phrase: 履歴書 / 職務経歴書
phrases.english_concept: CV / résumé — the Japanese document convention
phrases.usage_guidance: If Japanese copy ever touches job documents, name both and treat them as the maximally decoration-hostile surface. This is the register boundary for the whole Japanese professional family — the exact counterpart of German 'tabellarischer Lebenslauf' (P3).
phrases.good_example: 職務経歴・自己PRの登録内容が文字化けします。
phrases.avoid_when: Never mix with JA aesthetic/subculture vocabulary (JA-016 量産型, JA-017 地雷系, JA-029 ギャル文字) — the register clash would be severe. Do not translate 'resume' as レジュメ in this context without care; レジュメ in Japanese often means a meeting handout.

phrases.english_concept: Recency is baked into the JA query
phrases.usage_guidance: Signals that JA users expect a freshness claim, not just a character list
phrases.avoid_when: Do not make a freshness claim the site cannot maintain

phrases.english_concept: JA users design *combinations* of combining marks to achieve a transparent name
phrases.usage_guidance: Only relevant to JA; this technique does not generalise
phrases.avoid_when: Do not present as the standard method on non-JA pages

phrases.content_surface: FAQ; H2 on ja game-name copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Strongly prefer the transparency framing in JA gaming copy

phrases.native_phrase: emoji combos + コピペ / 使い方 / 星
phrases.english_concept: English loanword head + native intent qualifier — a compound search-formulation pattern
phrases.content_surface: ja/ library collection page titles/meta and section headings
phrases.usage_guidance: Japanese users keep the English head term 'emoji combos' but append a NATIVE intent qualifier — コピペ (copy-paste), 使い方 (how to use), a subject like 星 (star), or a problem statement like うまくできない (can't get it right). The pattern to serve is loanword-head + native-qualifier, not a full Japanese translation of the head term.
phrases.good_example: GSC (Jul 22 - Aug 2 2026, Japan): 'emoji combos コピペ' 84 imp / 7 clicks / 8.3% CTR / pos 2.64; 'emoji combos 使い方' 28 imp / 2 clicks; 'emoji combos うまく できない' 37 imp / 2 clicks; 'emoji combos 星' 35 imp; '絵文字combo' 30 imp — all onto /ja/library/emoji-combos/
phrases.avoid_when: Do not render the head term as 絵文字の組み合わせ in title position on the assumption that native is better — the measured queries keep the loanword head. 絵文字 is fine in prose.

phrases.english_concept: emoji combination/pairing -- the natural conversational phrasing, distinct from the loanword head term JA-048 tracks
phrases.content_surface: ja/library/emoji-combos/ -- already present in the meta description, not in title/H1 (see JA-EV-071)
phrases.usage_guidance: Do NOT use to override JA-048s loanword-head finding for TITLE/H1 position -- raw GSC search volume still favors 絵文字コンボ/emoji combos. Candidate for snippet/meta-description and body-prose use, where it already partially appears, to better match how users actually describe wanting this when they are not typing a search-engine query.
phrases.good_example: かわいい絵文字の組み合わせ教えてください！
phrases.avoid_when: Do not promote to title/H1 on the assumption native phrasing outperforms loanword phrasing in raw volume -- it does not, per JA-048.

phrases.native_phrase: ディスプレイネームスタイル
phrases.english_concept: Discord's own Nitro-exclusive per-message display-name font/color feature -- a named product feature, not a generic decoration concept
phrases.usage_guidance: This is Discord's OWN built-in, PAID (Nitro-gated) feature -- not a copy-paste workaround. Relevant to ja/guide/discord-font-doko/ and ja/guide/discord-moji-soshoku/ as a contrast/FAQ angle ('here is Discord's native paid option; here is a free alternative that needs no Nitro'), not as a term to rank for directly -- it is Discord's own product name, not user search vocabulary.
phrases.good_example: 様々なフォントや色で自分の名前を装飾出来る機能です。
phrases.avoid_when: Do not present UTG as replicating this exact in-app feature -- it is a different mechanism (in-message rendered font, Nitro-gated) vs. UTG's copy-paste display-name decoration (plain Unicode substitution, free, works everywhere).

phrases.usage_guidance: JA search separates 記号 (typographic glyph: 音楽 記号 33,100, 星 記号 1,300, 三角 記号 720) from 絵文字 (true emoji: 泣く 絵文字 8,100, 手 絵文字 2,900). Pick by what the page actually renders, not by what the EN title says.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not map an EN page titled "…Emoji" onto 絵文字 automatically — check whether its tiles are Unicode glyphs (記号) or emoji.
